Measures
In this BFI data set, the 5 factors refer to the 5 composites included in the Big Five Inventory. Openness, which indicates one’s open-mindedness, creativity, and likelihood to embrace new experiences (Cronbach’s alpha = 0.6). Conscientiousness, which refers to one’s tendency to be reliable, organized, and disciplined (Cronbach’s alpha = 0.72). Extraversion, which refers to one’s social interactions and emotional expression (Cronbach’s alpha = 0.76). Agreeableness, which refers to one’s tendency to cooperate or desire to compete (Cronbach’s alpha = 0.7). and Neuroticism which refers to one’s tendency toward depression, anxiety, or negative feelings (Cronbach’s alpha =0.81).


Data Analysis Strategy
The data for variables O2, C4, E1, E2, and A1 were reverse keyed.

title: 9041 Assignment 2
text: The present study sought to explore attachment and social anxiety.

title: 9041 Assignment 2
text:
Methods
Participants were recruited via the University of Edinburgh’s online learning portal and social media platforms, as well as through word-of-mouth. A flyer with a link to the study was shared on these platforms along with a standard message explaining the purpose of the study, the inclusion criteria (i.e., must be over the age of 18), and the contact details of one of the researchers. The participants followed a link to the questionnaire, which was created using the Online Surveys platform. Participants responded to 3 questionnaires to measure 1) Attachment-related anxiety, 2) Social anxiety and 3) Self-esteem. They were also asked to report their gender, age group, relationship status and ethnicity.

title: 9041 Assignment 2
text:
Measures
The present study explored the outcomes of interest using the Social Interaction Anxiety Scale, a shortened version of the Attachment-Related Anxiety subscale of the Experiences in Close Relationships Scale, and Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale. Chronbach’s alpha were calculated for each scale, reporting good to excellent reliability , respectively.

title: 9041 Assignment 2
text:
Data Analysis Strategy
Following data collection, data was cleaned by converting survey responses to integers and coding all responses according to the procedures outlined by the scale developers. Items 5, 9, and 11 in the Social Interaction Anxiety Scale and items 2, 5, 6, 8, and 9 in the Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale were reverse coded. Answer keys were then developed in order to determine participant average scores across all 3 outcome variables.
